text.p: Latvian commercial bank Viktorija said on Monday it has launched lat-rouble futures trading on the St.Petersburg stock exchange.
The bank also said it was positive on getting approval from the Latvian central bank to have the derivatives trade recognised as a valid way of meeting central bank rules.

Viktorija has launched futures to cover its rouble positions, which according to Latvian central bank regulations cannot exceed 20 percent of the bank's own capital in total and 10 percent in a particular currency.
"I think that the answer of the central bank will be positive," Andris Linuzhs, investments manager of Viktorija Bank, told Reuters.
He said his bank was due tomorrow to meet central bank officials on the new derivatives products.
Viktorija sells the futures through a St.Petersburg investment company, Akvilon, a stock exchange member.
"Russian banks and investment companies which follow the movement of the lat and consider it stable enough take the lat risk and earn their comission," Linuzhs said.
The ratio of Viktorija's investments in Russia are currently bigger than allowed under central bank rules, he added.
"We are thus getting rid of our headaches at the moment, but provided the number of counter-agents in Russia is sufficient lat-rouble futures could turn into a trade in itself," Linuzhs said.
Viktorija is currently buying one lat June futures contract for 10,200 roubles per lat.
"It is basically an expression of trust into the current Russian and Latvian governments, as everybody knows that there is a corridor for the rouble," Linuzhs added.
